best_for: Windows users who would rather commit, pull and diff from right-click menus in File Explorer than learn Git commands.

points.title: Git from the Explorer menu
points.text: TortoiseGit adds a context menu for Git and status icons on your files in File Explorer. You stage, commit, diff and push without opening a terminal.

points.title: Install Git first
points.text: TortoiseGit needs a command-line Git that provides `git.exe`. The docs recommend Git for Windows; Cygwin and MSYS2 Git also work but are not officially supported. You can skip Git for Windows' own Explorer integration.

points.title: Windows 10 or later, with admin rights
points.text: It runs on Windows 10 or higher; Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 are no longer supported, and older releases remain for them. Installing needs administrator rights and the Visual C++ 2015-2022 redistributable.

points.title: Pick the right build
points.text: Installers come for 32-bit, 64-bit and Arm64 Windows, and the project warns setup fails if you choose the wrong one. Language packs are separate downloads that need the main program.

points.title: Free and GPL
points.text: TortoiseGit is open source under GPL-2.0 and costs nothing. The project asks for donations.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. The listing keeps 13 versions.
